fixes.explanation: Egypt it is, friend. The famine was severe, so Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while (Genesis 12:10). When my own cookie jar runs empty, I start eyeing other kitchens too. That's a very human reason to head somewhere new.

Abram doesn't mention going back at all. He says, "Then they will kill me but will let you live." (Genesis 12:12) That's a heavy thing to say. This part of the story is a tough one, so let's take it slowly.

The text never says the officials asked Abram anything. It says they "…commended her to him…" meaning to Pharaoh (Genesis 12:15). Commended means they spoke well of her. Abram isn't in that verse at all.

No warning here. The officials "…commended her to him…" which means they spoke well of her to Pharaoh (Genesis 12:15). A warning is the opposite of speaking well. So that's not the word the text gives us.

A temple would be a different place, but that's not what the text says. Sarai "…was taken into the palace of Pharaoh." (Genesis 12:15). Pharaoh is the king of Egypt, and the palace is his home. Temple is a good guess, but palace is the word.

That's the whole list, and it's a long one. Abram "…acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels." (Genesis 12:16) The verse before says Pharaoh treated Abram well on her account. My order forms never run that long, friend. I think this part makes the story feel heavy.

A seat at court never comes up. Abram "…acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels." (Genesis 12:16) That's animals and servants. No court seat is on the list.
